narrative_purpose: The cold-open anchor: a thanator over its kill that the eye reads as 'panther' before it notices the alien details, so the reader feels the chapter's central tension firsthand.
subject: A massive six-limbed black predator crouched low over a fallen prey animal in the forest gloom, its lean muscular body and grappling forelimbs reading unmistakably as a great cat mid-feed. On closer look it is alien: six limbs, a flared armoured crest behind the skull, four forward eyes in two stacked pairs, and faint bioluminescent striping along its flanks. A clear dark region of empty forest sits to the upper left of the animal.
scene: Deep bioluminescent understory at night, glowing ferns and fungal light low to the ground, heavy haze swallowing the background.
camera: Low naturalist three-quarter view, slightly below the predator, prey beneath its forelimbs.
light: Faint cyan glow from ground flora rim-lighting the crouched body; the predator mostly in indigo shadow; eyes catching a scarce cool glint.
palette: Void indigo and ocean teal dominant, cyan rim light, one scarce magenta glint in the eyes.
style: Hand-painted naturalist plate, textured and observed.
detail_level: High on the predator and its head; soft on the hazy surround.
composition: Predator crouched centre-right over prey, open dark hazy negative space upper-left for a callout, depth dissolving behind.
consistency_notes: Same thanator archetype as fig-00 and fig-02. Leave the upper-left dark for annotation.
